correctness.rationale: Exact de Finetti mixture and fixed-bias gambler ruin give P(N>=k|Theta)=(1-|2Theta-1|)^k; Laplace concentration and Scheffe yield the total-variation latent posterior; conditional renewal gives independent geometric remaining returns; the defective first-return PGF 1-sqrt(1-4pq z^2) yields a uniformly convergent compact-scaled conditional epoch transform exp(x-sqrt(x^2+2s)); the exponential drift mixture has inverse-exponential density e^{-1/(2t)}/(2t^2). The proof covers all real fixed a,b>0 and specifies conditioning and scope. The standalone checker reproduces 2,335 exact/numerical assertions.

originality.rationale: Comparative assessment credits the exact 2014 finite indexed-tie kernels and established duration/intensity asymptotics, and does not call their marginals new. Full mathematical novelty claimed is the simultaneous conditional scaling of the latent directing drift, k-th return epoch, and future-return mark across all fixed positive initial masses, with a specific mixed Brownian hitting-time and independence coupling. Primary full text and published-finding corpus searches found no directly asserting or straightforwardly dominating joint theorem; genuinely material residual priority risks remain.
residual_risks: The 2014 indexed-tie formulas give exact finite statistics that can imply some balanced special-case timing marginals after asymptotic analysis.
Other conditioned-renewal or random-drift mixture limit theorems, not found in searches, may imply the joint statement.
Complete material for Antal et al. 2010 and Mookerjee/Kostinski 2024 was not inspected; any strong equivalence would require further independent review.

value.rationale: The joint limit resolves the natural relationship among hidden bias selected by many returns, the quadratic time of the k-th return, and the number of returns left. The universal inverse-exponential clock with an explicit drift-conditioned Brownian first-passage law and an independent future-count mark conditional on the drift is a structural rare-event law rather than a random finite slice, simple tail recomputation or trivial algebraic renaming. It refines separate known duration and intensity tails.
